newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Aug 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Aug 17.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
A flash flood, triggered by incessant railfall and on-rush of waters from hills in India, on Saturday inundated vast areas in northern districts.
The World Bank warns fiscal balances are likely to come under greater pressure in fiscal 1997/98 (July-June) because of salary increases of government employees.

Upendra Lal Chakma, leader of tribal refugees living in camps in Indian state of Tripura, has said refugees are unwilling to return home as they no more believe that they will be treated as "sons of the soil."
Former President and opposition Jatiya Party chief Hussain Muhammad Ershad is due to return home on Sunday after a month-long trip to Saudi Arabia, Britain and India.
Singapore-based Chittagong Feeder Trade Committee has imposed congestion surcharge at Chittagong Port from Sunday.
Workers and employees of river vessels is due to begin strike for indefinite period on Sunday to demand higher wage.
The giant multinational fetrilitiser industry, Kafco, suffered a loss of over $100 million during the last two-and-a-half year due to malfunctioning of its plant in Chittagong.
Noted economist and former finance adviser of the caretaker government, Dr Wahiduddin Mahmud, has been appointed as the chairman of the Banking Reforms Commission. REUTER
